outcome: As of 13 Oct 2026 no source I could read says the conjecture is settled; Wikipedia, Feofiloff's notes and the 2025–26 Cornuéjols–Liu–Ravi papers all still list it as open. Since 26 Jan 2024 the non-AI literature has added partial and restricted results (a p-adic relaxation, a dyadic blow-up relaxation, the weighted Edmonds–Giles statement for chordal underlying graphs, a dual form for 3-trees). In September 2026 a public repository run by AI agents posted merged, sketch-status proofs for the τ=2 case (folklore) and for τ=3 special classes, reviewed only by other AI models.
problem_asks: One statement, two quantities, for every digraph (read as finite, unweighted, with a dicut present): (1) τ(D), the minimum number of arcs in a non-empty dicut (a dicut is a non-empty arc set δ+(U) with no arcs entering U); and (2) ν(D), the maximum number of pairwise disjoint dijoins (a dijoin meets every non-empty dicut; equivalently its contraction makes D strongly connected). The conjecture asks that τ(D) = ν(D) for all D. Unpacked: (a) ν(D) ≤ τ(D) is immediate, because each dijoin must contain an arc of a smallest dicut and disjoint dijoins need distinct arcs; (b) the open content is ν(D) ≥ τ(D), i.e. every digraph has τ(D) pairwise disjoint dijoins, for every value of τ. The statement is the unweighted case; the weighted Edmonds–Giles form (refuted by Schrijver, 1980) is a different statement. Reading note: the statement must use the non-empty-dicut convention; a permissive empty-dicut convention makes τ=0 and trivialises small-case checks (see the repo issue #295 discussed below).

events.what_happened: Chudnovsky, Edwards, Kim, Scott and Seymour, ‘Disjoint dijoins’ (arXiv 1412.1415, one version). Restates Woodall’s conjecture, says it ‘remains open, but a capacitated version is known to be false’, and proves a k=2 statement about a connected subdigraph S (if S is connected and every dicut has at least two arcs of S, S splits into two dijoins) only when G is planar or S is a subdivided caterpillar. Predates the window.
events.revisions: v1 only, submitted 3 Dec 2014 (arXiv abstract page).
events.delivers: Two special cases of a connectivity-conditioned k=2 statement about a subdigraph S: G planar; or S a subdivided caterpillar. The plain k=2 case of Woodall is folklore (Wikipedia), so this does not add a new k=2 case for general digraphs.
events.remains: Woodall for general digraphs and all k≥3. A search summary of the introduction (not the abstract) says the k=3 case is open even for planar digraphs.
events.direction: Partial: confirms the k=2 instance inside two classes and clarifies the capacitated counterexample. Does not cut against the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Gollin, Heuer and Stavropoulos, ‘Disjoint dijoins for classes of dicuts in finite and infinite digraphs’ (arXiv 2109.03518). Asks a modified question: for a restricted class of dicuts, is the maximum number of disjoint sets meeting every dicut of the class equal to the minimum size of a dicut in the class? Verifies it for nested classes of finite dicuts, for the class of minimum-size dicuts, and for classes of infinite dibonds. Predates the window.
events.revisions: v1 only, submitted 8 Sep 2021 (arXiv abstract page).

events.remains: The statement for all dicuts of a finite digraph; the infinite-digraph setting is outside the bullet.
events.doubts: A variant with a weaker packing requirement; success on the variant is not evidence on the original statement.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture on the classes treated; a variant, not the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Schrijver, ‘A counterexample to a conjecture of Edmonds and Giles’, Discrete Mathematics 32(2):213–215 (per Wikipedia’s reference list). Refutes the weighted (capacitated) Edmonds–Giles conjecture. Not an event on the unweighted statement.
events.delivers: Refutes the weighted Edmonds–Giles form in general. Its planar digraph has an arc subset S in which every dicut contains at least two arcs of S, yet S contains no two disjoint dijoins. The sources treat this as a capacitated counterexample, not a counterexample to the unweighted statement.
events.remains: Woodall’s unweighted statement, which every source read treats as open.

events.what_happened: Lee and Williams, ‘Packing dicycle covers in planar graphs with no K5−e minor’, LATIN 2006, pp. 677–688 (per the LATIN bibliography entry and a Springer abstract reported in search results). events.what_happened: Cornuéjols, Liu and Ravi, ‘Approximately packing dijoins via nowhere-zero flows’ (arXiv 2311.04337). Main result: if the underlying undirected graph of a digraph with minimum dicut size τ admits a nowhere-zero circular k-flow, the digraph has ⌊τ/k⌋ disjoint dijoins. Seymour’s nowhere-zero 6-flow theorem gives ⌊τ/6⌋ disjoint dijoins for every digraph, findable in polynomial time; 6p-edge-connected underlying graphs give ⌊τp/(2p+1)⌋. The paper was an IPCO 2024 paper (LNCS 14679, pp. 71–84, per its own reference list); Wikipedia cites a Combinatorica 2025 journal version (DOI 10.1007/s00493-025-00159-x in search results; the Springer page was not readable to me). Version 2 also reformulates the conjecture via strongly connected orientations and states it holds for τ=2.
events.revisions: v1 submitted 7 Nov 2023; v2 22 May 2025 (arXiv). IPCO 2024 conference version; journal version reported as Combinatorica 2025 (not verified).
events.delivers: A fractional-type bound: ν(D) ≥ ⌊τ/k⌋ under a flow condition, and ν(D) ≥ ⌊τ/6⌋ for all digraphs. Each is a fixed fraction of τ and so does not reach ν=τ. The τ=2 case is covered (folklore).
events.remains: Exact equality ν = τ for all digraphs and all τ≥3; closing the gap between τ/6 and τ (the authors say reaching ⌊τ/2⌋ would need new ideas, per a summary of v2).

events.what_happened: Bertrand Guenin, ‘A relaxation of Woodall’s conjecture’, University of Waterloo Graphs and Matroids seminar, Tuesday 2 July 2024 (joint with Steven Hwang). The talk abstract claims that for every digraph there is an integer k such that, after replacing each edge by 2^k parallel copies, Woodall’s minimax relation holds. Published as Guenin and Hwang, ‘Dyadic packing of dijoins’, SIAM Journal on Discrete Mathematics 39(1):593–606 (2025), DOI 10.1137/24M1647692, which per its search-result abstract shows that every integer-weighted digraph has a maximum fractional packing of dijoins with dyadic values, and presents this as settling Seymour’s dyadic conjecture for dijoin clutters. I found no arXiv preprint. The first written argument is not located; the talk abstract is the earliest dated public statement I found.
events.revisions: No arXiv preprint found. SIAM journal version 2025 (page returned 403; abstract from search metadata). If a written preprint predates 26 Jan 2024, the date moves earlier; not established.
events.delivers: A relaxation: after 2^k parallel copies of each edge (k depending on the digraph), Woodall’s minimax relation holds. The journal version gives a maximum fractional packing with dyadic values for the original digraph, not an integral packing.
events.remains: The integral packing of τ disjoint dijoins in the original digraph, i.e. the conjecture itself.

events.what_happened: Juan Gutiérrez (Alva), ‘Towards a conjecture of Woodall for partial 3-trees’ (arXiv 2408.05703 v1, 11 Aug 2024), retitled ‘Towards a Dual Version of Woodall’s Conjecture for Partial 3-Trees’ (v2, 10 Sep 2025). Addresses the dual formulation: for planar digraphs, the introduction says ‘by duality, Conjecture 1 is equivalent to asserting that, for every planar digraph, its girth equals the cardinality of a maximum packing’ (shortest dicycle versus disjoint feedback arc sets). Main theorem (v2, Theorem 2): if G has a dicycle and its underlying graph is a 3-tree then the dual equality holds, and the paper notes this is valid even if G is not planar. Corollary for partial 3-trees of girth 3. Also a tight bound: every 3-tree has a feedback arc set of at most m/3−1 arcs.
events.revisions: v1 11 Aug 2024 (title ‘Towards a conjecture of Woodall for partial 3-trees’, framed for planar 3-trees per my search summary); v2 10 Sep 2025 (retitled; Theorem 2 extended to all 3-trees, not only planar).
events.delivers: The dual (dicycle/feedback-arc-set) equality for digraphs whose underlying graph is a 3-tree, and for partial 3-trees of girth 3. For planar digraphs the dual is equivalent to the dicut/dijoin statement, so the planar subcase transfers. For non-planar 3-trees the paper’s text does not show equivalence to the dicut/dijoin statement.
events.remains: The dicut/dijoin statement for all digraphs; the dual statement outside 3-trees and partial 3-trees of girth 3; the dual for planar digraphs in general.
events.doubts: No journal record or citing publication found in my searches; not peer reviewed as far as I found. Scope changed between versions: v1 described a planar 3-tree case; v2 claims all 3-trees, so the planar duality that ties the dual form to Woodall covers only part of the stated class.
events.direction: Supports the dual form on the stated class; no counterexample.
events.object: Feedback arc sets in 3-trees: a tight bound of m/3−1 on the minimum feedback arc set size (m = number of arcs), with the bound attained. Not a counterexample to anything.

events.what_happened: Cornuéjols, Liu and Ravi, ‘A min-max relation on dicuts and dijoins in weighted chordal digraphs’ (arXiv 2501.10918). Theorem 1.1: the Edmonds–Giles conjecture holds for digraphs whose underlying undirected graph is chordal. The conjecture as the paper states it: in a weighted digraph the minimum weight of a dicut equals the maximum size of a packing of dijoins, with no arc e in more than w(e) members (integral). The paper also gives a strongly polynomial algorithm for the packing. Published in Journal of Graph Theory (2026, DOI 10.1002/jgt.70076 per search result; Wiley page returned 403).
events.delivers: The weighted Edmonds–Giles statement for chordal underlying graphs. With unit weights the statement is exactly Woodall’s for digraphs with chordal underlying graph. That specialisation is my inference from the stated packing definition; the paper does not draw it, and states that the unweighted version of Edmonds–Giles, ‘proposed by Woodall’, ‘is still open’.
events.remains: Woodall’s statement for digraphs whose underlying graph is not chordal (the general case, per the authors’ own statement).

disputes.summary: Cornuéjols–Liu–Ravi (arXiv 2311.04337): Wikipedia cites Combinatorica 45(3) (2025); the arXiv version and its reference list cite IPCO 2024 (LNCS 14679, pp. 71–84). A Springer DOI with the Combinatorica prefix appears in search results, but I could not open it. Unresolved.

The chordal weighted Edmonds–Giles theorem (arXiv 2501.10918) appears to give Woodall’s unweighted statement for chordal underlying graphs when all weights are 1. The authors state that the unweighted version remains open. My reading of the packing definition may differ from theirs; unresolved.

Lee–Williams planar result: sources disagree on the excluded minor, K5−e (dicycle-cover form, Springer abstract as reported in search) or the triangular prism (dijoin form, per arXiv 2109.03518). The two are planar duals of each other; which form is stated is unresolved.

PR #159 presents a self-contained proof of the τ=2 case. Wikipedia describes the τ=2 case as folklore. The repo does not claim the case is new in the sources read, but the write-up is a sketch, reviewed only by AI models.
Abdi–Cornuéjols–Zlatin: search summaries say v1 stated a partition into a k-dijoin and a (τ−k)-dijoin for every k when w≡1; the v5 abstract states only k=1. The v1 PDF was not opened.
The 2^k blow-up relaxation (Guenin talk, July 2024; Guenin–Hwang SIAM 2025) may overlap with Hwang’s 2022 Waterloo thesis on relaxations of the Edmonds–Giles conjecture. The thesis was not read.

summary: Woodall’s conjecture is still open on every source I could read: the Wikipedia article (lead: ‘an unproven relationship between dicuts and dijoins’), Feofiloff’s USP pages (updated 2026-08-18, no new results listed), and the 2025–26 Cornuéjols–Liu–Ravi papers, which state that the unweighted version remains open. The events since 26 January 2024 are restricted or relaxed results. Cornuéjols–Liu–Ravi’s nowhere-zero-flow bound ⌊τ/6⌋ (preprint Nov 2023, before the window; IPCO 2024; journal 2025) is an approximate fraction of τ. Abdi–Cornuéjols–Liu–Silina (Oct 2024) gives a p-adic relaxation. Guenin’s talk (July 2024), published with Hwang in SIAM 2025, gives a dyadic/blow-up relaxation. Gutiérrez (Aug 2024, v2 Sep 2025) proves a dual feedback-arc-set form for 3-trees; I found no peer review. The chordal Edmonds–Giles theorem (Jan 2025, JGT 2026) is the closest to a class-level settlement: with unit weights it appears to give Woodall for chordal underlying graphs, though the authors say the unweighted version is open, which I could not reconcile from the readable text. The AI search found one substantial source. A public GitHub repository (SzymonPawlus/clanker-solving-riemman-hypothesis-inator, README: ‘Two LLM agents — Claude and Codex — attacking open mathematical problems’) posted, between 2 and 7 Sep 2026, Woodall proofs by AI agents. PR #159 gives a τ=2 proof (folklore; merged 4 Sep, labelled ‘sketch’, with its load-bearing Schrijver filter step unreconstructed by the author). PRs #210, #215 and #216 give τ=3 special classes and class-restricted arbitrary-k and closure results (each merged 4 Sep after approval by a Claude review, with no human mathematical review found). About 58 Woodall-titled PRs exist, most still open or changes-requested with specific defects, and issue #295 says the repo’s own exact-search tool misstated its coverage. None of the mainstream papers names an AI system in the text I could read. The close calls are: whether the chordal unit-weight case counts as a class-level settlement; whether the 2024 blow-up is priority-novel given Hwang’s thesis; and whether AI-only-reviewed class results count as a case settled before any human reading. The τ=2 case is folklore, so PR #159 adds write-up, not a new case. I record these as events and leave the weighing to the judging pass.
competing_reading: Read the chordal Edmonds–Giles theorem with unit weights as settling Woodall for chordal underlying graphs, so that a class-level case has been settled by a peer-reviewed JGT paper. Against that: the authors say the unweighted version is open, and their definition may differ from mine. Read the repository results as sketch-status arguments from AI agents with no human check, so that none counts as settling any case; against that: PRs #210, #215 and #216 are class-restricted claims that would be new if correct, and they were merged after approval by a second model.
what_would_settle_it: The full PDF text of arXiv 2501.10918 (the definition of the packing and whether Theorem 1.1 covers w≡1), and the JGT version. The Combinatorica 2025 record for 2311.04337. The SIAM 2025 paper of Guenin and Hwang and any earlier preprint, with the date of the first written argument. The v1 PDF of arXiv 2202.00392 (the ‘every k’ claim). Hwang’s 2022 thesis, to settle priority of the relaxation. Raw, unsummarised GitHub pages for PRs #159, #210, #215, #216 and their review bodies, to confirm the quotes. Any Lean sorry-free proof of the τ=2 or τ=3 arguments. A named human expert (for example Cornuéjols, Abdi, Seymour or Feofiloff) reading the repository’s claims.

incomplete: (1) GitHub was read only through the web fetch tool, which summarises pages. The quotes attributed to the repository (commit trailers, review sentences, PR descriptions) come from those summaries and must be checked against the raw pages; the gh CLI was blocked by the approval gate. (2) About 58 Woodall-titled PRs and 79 issues exist; I read the review journals and roughly fifteen PRs and issues in detail. The other PRs are summarised only by their titles and listing states, and the attack PRs (#219–#257 and others) have not been opened individually. (3) The repository’s results file (problems/woodalls-conjecture/results/woodall-lean-basics.md) and the Lean files under lean/Verified/Woodall/ were not read. (4) Not read: the full text of the Springer/Combinatorica version of 2311.04337 (403/redirect); the Wiley JGT version of 2501.10918 (403); the SIAM version of Guenin–Hwang (403); the Lee–Wakabayashi 2001 and Feofiloff–Younger 1987 papers (not accessible); the Schrijver 1980 and 1982 papers; the Lee–Williams 2006 paper; Hwang’s 2022 thesis; the v1 PDF of 2202.00392; the full body of 2501.10918 (PDF compressed; only HTML main theorem and introduction read); the body of 2310.19472 (abstract only, via a summariser); the body of 2109.03518 and 1412.1415 (abstracts only); the acknowledgements of 2410.13665 (cut off). (5) Feofiloff’s 2025 series-parallel draft and survey PDFs were unreadable; Liu’s 2025 proposal was unreadable. (6) I did not establish the first public written argument for the Guenin–Hwang blow-up result; the talk abstract (2 Jul 2024) is the earliest dated statement I found. (7) Pre-window results were searched through the abstract and secondary citations, not full texts. (8) The AI search covered the named labs and tracker sites through search only; I did not check the Erdős problems database, the Open Problem Garden comment history, or the formal-conjectures repository.
